title: Consistency of AI-driven analysis of consecutively taken bitewing images with Nostic. A retrospective analysis.
summary: Bitewing radiographs are used to diagnose and monitor caries in the approximal (interdental) areas. These images can also be automatically analyzed using AI-based software. In routine clinical practice, however, bitewing radiographs often vary in image quality and projection angle, which can complicate assessment. In this retrospective study, anonymized bitewing radiographs from the same patients at two time points (T0 and T1) are evaluated to determine whether an AI system can reliably re-detect caries findings on follow-up images and thus support caries monitoring over time. In addition, the AI results are compared with the findings of human examiners.
conditions: Caries Diagnosis on Radiographs – A Retrospective Analysis

interventions.name: Assessment of anonymized bitewing radiographs (T0/T1) using an AI-assisted analysis (Nostic) on approximal surfaces (mesial/distal) according to D0–D4; analysis performed blinded following randomized renaming/permutation of the image files.

Independent assessment of the same anonymised bitewing radiographs by human examiners—two per study centre plus one additional examiner from a dental practice—at proximal tooth surfaces (mesial/distal) using the D0–D4 classification. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients are included if two consecutive bitewing radiographs (T0 and T1) are available. At T0, at least two non-restored approximal surfaces (mesial or distal) must be present.
Exclusion criteria:
No exclusion criteria are defined.
